name: SikaWrap-300 C
paste:
SIKAWRAP®-300 C: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: SikaWrap®-300 C, April 2023, Version 01.02 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/o/sikawrap_-300_c.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide SikaWrap®-300 C where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02).
1.2 Product description. SikaWrap®-300 C is a unidirectional woven carbon fibre fabric with mid-range strengths, designed for installation using the dry or wet application process.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. SikaWrap®-300 C may only be used by experienced professionals. Structural strengthening of reinforced concrete, masonry, brickwork and timber elements or structures, to increase flexural and shear loading capacity for:
    - Improved seismic performance of masonry walls
    - Replacing missing steel reinforcement
    - Increasing the strength and ductility of columns
    - Increasing the loading capacity of structural elements
    - Enabling changes in use / alterations and refurbishment
    - Correcting structural design and / or construction defects
    - Increasing resistance to seismic movement
    - Improving service life and durability
    - Structural upgrading to comply with current standards
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.5.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. SikaWrap®-300 C
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: Woven unidirectional carbon fibre fabric, designed for structural strengthening applications as part of the Sika® strengthening system.
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals / certificates.
    - Australia: AS5100.8:2017
    - Australia: Vic Roads Section 688
    - USA: ACI 440.2R-08, Guide for the Design and construction of Externally Bonded FRP Systems for strengthening concrete structures, July 2008
    - UK: Concrete Society Technical Report No. 55, Design guidance for strengthening concrete structures using fibre composite material, 2012.
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - AS5100.8:2017: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - ISO 10618: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Dry fibre elongation at break (p.2); Product Information > Dry fibre modulus of elasticity in tension (p.2); Product Information > Dry fibre tensile strength (p.2).
    - EN 2561: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Laminate elongation at break in tension 1.56 % (p.2); Technical Information > Laminate modulus of elasticity in tension (p.2); Technical Information > Laminate tensile strength (p.2); Technical Information > Tensile resistance (p.2); Technical Information > Tensile stiffness (p.2).
    - ASTM D 3039: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Laminate elongation at break in tension 1.56 % (p.2); Technical Information > Laminate modulus of elasticity in tension (p.2); Technical Information > Laminate tensile strength (p.2).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Multifunctional fabric for use in many different strengthening applications
    - Flexible and accommodating to different surface planes and geometry (beams, columns, chimneys, piles, walls, soffits, silos etc.)
    - Low density for minimal additional weight
    - Extremely cost effective in comparison to traditional strengthening techniques
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Dry fibre density: 1.82 g/cm³
2.6 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Fibre type: Selected mid-range strength carbon fibres
    - Mass per area: 304 g/m² ±10 g/m² (carbon fibres only)
    - Dry fibre tensile strength: 4 000 N/mm² (ISO 10618)
    - Dry fibre modulus of elasticity in tension: 230 000 N/mm² (ISO 10618)
    - Dry fibre elongation at break: 1.7 % (ISO 10618)
    - Design nominal thickness: 0.167 mm
    - Design nominal cross section: 167 mm²per m width
    - Laminate elongation at break in tension 1.56 %: 1.59 % (based on EN 2561) (based on ASTM D 3039)

2.12 System structure. The system build-up and configuration as described must be fully complied with and may not be changed.
    | Concrete substrate adhesive primer | Sikadur®-330 |
    | Impregnating / laminating resin | Sikadur®-330 or Sikadur®-300 |
    | Structural strengthening fabric | SikaWrap®-300 C |
    (System build-up table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows. Refer to the data sheet (page 2) for the layout.)
    For detailed information on Sikadur®-330 or Sikadur®-300, together with the resin and fabric application details, please refer to the Sikadur®-330 or Sikadur®-300 Product Data Sheet and the relevant Method Statement.
2.13 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Shelf life: 24 months from date of production
    - Storage conditions: Store in undamaged, original sealed packaging, in dry conditions at temperatures between +5 °C and +35 °C. Protect from direct sunlight.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality.
    - Minimum substrate tensile strength: 1.0 N/mm² or as specified in the strengthening design.
    - Please also refer to the relevant Method Statement for further information..
3.3 Substrate preparation. Concrete must be cleaned and prepared to achieve a laitance and contaminant free, open textured surface. Please also refer to the relevant Method Statement for further information.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Dry fibre thickness: 0.167 mm (based on fibre content)
4.3 Consumption. Dry application with Sikadur®-330
    | First layer including primer layer | 1.0–1.5 kg/m² |
    | Following layers | 0.8 kg/m² |
    | Wet application with Sikadur®-300, primer Sikadur®-330 |
    | Primer layer | 0.4–0.6 kg/m² |
    | Fabric layers | 0.6 kg/m² |
    | Please also refer to the relevant Method Statement for further information. |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
4.4 Application method / tools.
    - The fabric can be cut with special scissors or a Stanley knife (razor knife / box-cutter knife). Never fold the fabric.
    - SikaWrap®-300 C is applied using the dry or wet application process.
    - Please refer to the relevant Method Statement for details on the impregnating / laminating procedure.
4.5 Limitations and important considerations.
    - SikaWrap®-300 C shall only be applied by trained and experienced professionals.
    - A specialist structural engineer must be consulted for any structural strengthening design calculation.
    - SikaWrap®-300 C fabric is coated to ensure maximum bond and durability with the Sikadur® adhesives / impregnating / laminating resins. To maintain and ensure full system compatibility, do not interchange different system components.
    - SikaWrap®-300 C can be over coated with a cementitious overlay or other coatings for aesthetic and / or protective purposes. The over coating system selection is dependent on the exposure and the project specific requirements. For additional UV light protection in exposed areas use Sikagard®-550 W Elastic, Sikagard® ElastoColor-675 W or Sikagard®-680 S.
    - Please refer to the Method Statement of SikaWrap® manual dry application (Ref. 850 41 02), SikaWrap® manual wet application (Ref. 850 41 03) or SikaWrap® machine wet application (Ref. 850 41 04) for further information, guidelines and limitations.
4.6 Further information - Method Statements. Ref. 850 41 02: SikaWrap® manual dry application Ref. 850 41 03: SikaWrap® manual wet application Ref. 850 41 04: SikaWrap® machine wet application

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, confirm the site conditions with the manufacturer. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Conditions to be verified. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (April 2023, Version 01.02) lists no application condition limits.
5.3 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Dry fibre tensile strength: 4 000 N/mm² (ISO 10618)
    - Dry fibre modulus of elasticity in tension: 230 000 N/mm² (ISO 10618)
    - Dry fibre elongation at break: 1.7 % (ISO 10618)
    - Laminate tensile strength: Average | Characteristic; 3 500 N/mm² | 3 200 kN/mm² (EN 2561*) (ASTM D 3039*)
    - Laminate modulus of elasticity in tension: Average | Characteristic; 225 kN/mm² | 220 kN/mm²; Average | Characteristic; 220 kN/mm² | 210 kN/mm² (EN 2561*) (ASTM D 3039*)
    - Laminate elongation at break in tension 1.56 %: 1.59 % (based on EN 2561) (based on ASTM D 3039)
    - Tensile resistance: Average | Characterstic; 585 N/mm | 534 N/mm (based on EN 2561) (based on ASTM D 3039)
    - Tensile stiffness: Average | Characteristic; 37.6 MN/m | 36.7 MN/m; 37.6 kN/m per ‰ elonga- | 36.7 kN/m per ‰ elonga-; tion | tion; Average | Characteristic; 36.7 MN/m | 35.1 MN/m; 36.7 kN/m per ‰ elonga- | 35.1 kN/m per ‰ elonga-; tion | tion (based on EN 2561) (based no ASTM D 3039)
5.4 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.5 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: SikaWrap®-300 C, April 2023, Version 01.02, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/o/sikawrap_-300_c.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety - Regulation (ec) no 1907/2006 - reach. This product is an article as defined in article 3 of regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 (REACH). It contains no substances which are intended to be released from the article under normal or reasonably foreseeable conditions of use. A safety data sheet following article 31 of the same regulation is not needed to bring the product to the market, to transport or to use it. For safe use follow the instructions given in the product data sheet. Based on our current knowledge, this product does not contain SVHC (substances of very high concern) as listed in Annex XIV of the REACH regulation or on the candidate list published by the European Chemicals Agency in concentrations above 0,1 % (w/w).
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.1, and include the records in the project documentation.
